definitions.gloss: organization; systematization; structuring into a system
definitions.explanation: The process of arranging people, activities, or information into a structured, organized system. Also refers to forming or unifying a group into an organized body.

examples.japanese: {労働者|ろうどうしゃ}の{組織化|そしきか}が{進|すす}んだ。
{情報|じょうほう}の{組織化|そしきか}は{業務|ぎょうむ}{効率|こうりつ}を{上|あ}げる。
ボランティア{活動|かつどう}を{組織化|そしきか}することで、より{効果的|こうかてき}な{支援|しえん}が{可能|かのう}になった。
examples.english: By organizing volunteer activities, more effective support became possible.

notes:
A compound of {組織|そしき} (organization) and {化|か} (the suffix meaning "-ization, turning into"). Describes the process of bringing order and structure to something that was previously unstructured.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {組織化|そしきか}する: to organize, to systematize
- {組織化|そしきか}された: organized, structured
- {組織化|そしきか}が{進|すす}む: organization progresses
- {組織化|そしきか}を{図|はか}る: to aim for organization

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {体系化|たいけいか}: systematization — emphasizes creating a logical system or framework
- {制度化|せいどか}: institutionalization — making something into an official system or institution
- {組織|そしき}: organization — the result (a structured body), not the process of creating one
